title: MedCLIP: Contrastive Learning from Unpaired Medical Images and Text
layout_note: Two dashed boxes on top (medical image datasets, medical text datasets); below, one framed region for image-text datasets in which an anchor X-ray with its report (left) and a negative X-ray with its report (right) are linked to a central circle.
grouping: Dashed boxes for each data source; a solid frame for the paired data; the true positive and the false negative in their own dashed columns with coloured captions.
shapes_depth: Real X-rays, report text with highlighted keywords, a grey sphere for the embedding space.
proposed_highlight: The problem (false negatives) is shown on real data with the shared keywords highlighted.
lesson: Show a supervision problem on two real image-report pairs with the words they share highlighted, instead of describing it.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue EMNLP 2022 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15).

arrangement.units: the unpaired sources in a top row; the paired data below in one frame with two dashed columns
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-rays and quoted report sentences with keywords highlighted
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; positive / negative captions under each column

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
